The schedule is unique. I re-derived it and checked all 17 constraints.

**Why Ben must be in slot 5:** Finn, Ivo, Hana and Gus all come before Ben, so he is at slot 5 or later. Ann is directly after him, and Cara comes after Ann, so Ben is at slot 7 or earlier. Elif comes right after Cara and Dev after Elif, which pushes Ben to slot 5 at most. So Ben is 5, Ann 6, and Cara, Elif and Dev take 7, 8 and 9 (Elif must be 8 to be two slots from Ann).

**Slots 1–4:** Finn and Gus must be three apart, which leaves only {1, 4}. Finn must precede Hana and Gus must precede Ben, so Finn is 1 and Gus is 4. Ivo and Hana are then in 2 and 3, and Hana is immediately after Ivo, so Ivo is 2 and Hana is 3.

**Check against all 17 constraints:**
- Finn(1) < Ben(5), Finn(1) < Ann(6), Finn(1) < Hana(3)
- Elif(8) < Dev(9)
- Ann(6) = Ben(5) + 1
- Ivo(2) < Gus(4), Gus(4) < Ben(5), Hana(3) < Ben(5)
- |Cara(7) − Gus(4)| = 3
- Elif(8) = Cara(7) + 1
- |Elif(8) − Ivo(2)| = 6
- Hana(3) = Ivo(2) + 1
- |Finn(1) − Gus(4)| = 3
- |Dev(9) − Finn(1)| = 8
- Ann(6) is two slots from Elif(8), with Cara(7) between them
- Ann(6) < Cara(7)
- |Ann(6) − Hana(3)| = 3

All hold, and the nine names are each used once.

My earlier explanation was looser than this derivation (it said slot 6 forces Elif into 9, which isn't quite the argument), but the schedule itself is the same and correct.

SCHEDULE: {"1":"Finn","2":"Ivo","3":"Hana","4":"Gus","5":"Ben","6":"Ann","7":"Cara","8":"Elif","9":"Dev"}
CONFIDENCE: 99
